description.narrative:
Strengthening the capacity of LEG for improved advocacy
Ghana, rich in minerals like gold, now leads gold production in Africa. The mining sector, providing jobs and state revenue, is significant for the economy. For instance, Newmont Ghana Gold Limited contributed over 843 million Ghana Cedis in early 2023 and 1.295 billion cedis in the first quarter of 2024 in taxes and royalties Yet, mining, particularly gold, brings severe social, environmental, and human rights issues. Ghana’s mining has been cited as a major human rights violator, causing displacement and poverty.
The sector is plagued by legal non-compliance, human rights abuses, property destruction without fair compensation, and environmental pollution. Despite this, few scientific studies have examined these abuses since reports by CHRAJ in 2008 and LEG in 2010. Additionally, digital communication, crucial for outreach and fundraising, is a skill gap among LEG’s staff and volunteers. This deficiency has kept two decades and has retired our development. Livelihood and Environment Ghana (LEG) is seeking a grant support of € 19,980 from MCS Fund to document human rights abuses, improve digital communication skills, and enhance fundraising for sustainability.
The fund would be used for the implementation of two related activities which together will strengthen the capacity of LEG, our community volunteers and F4All partners of Oxfam Ghana and TWN-Africa to contribute to ongoing advocacy for ending impunity in local communities. The firstactivity is evidenced-based research on human rights abuses incommunities affected by mining. The second activity is targeted capacity building and training on two areas: digital communication and fundraising.
All the two activities will be completedby the end of 2024. The results of the activities will continue to be used for a couple of years beyond as beneficiaries will be equipped with knowledge, skills and techniques for digital communication andfundraising. The research is expected to produce evidence/results that would stimulate continued advocacy on human rights. But the knowledge and skills acquired on digital communication will be sufficiently valuable for the implementation of aspects of research findings. In the implementation of the activities, LEG will work with researchers and community based volunteers from communities affected by mining and F4All partners in Ghana to improve coordinated campaigns while avoiding overlap and duplication in those communities.
The total funding beingsought for project is € 19,980 broken down as follows: 1. Research project - € 8,396 2. Capacity building and Training: a. Digital communication- €4,548 b. Fundraising – € 2,145 3. Advocacy and engagement - € 3,532 (launch of researchreport and advocacy engagements) 4. Administrative overheads cost- € 1,359
LEG is uniquely placed to implement this project and optimize the opportunities that this funding will offer. LEG’s long running involvement (2 decades) in community work and grassroots networking and advocacy on mining issues has enabled it develop experience and a range of relationships with variety of actors at thelocal level the type which is needed to best engage long after the implementation of the project.

participating-org.narrative:
Our vision To see a diverse environment where there is equity, inclusion and decentralized decision-making, free from all forms of impunity and human rights abuses and offers equal opportunity for all class of people and enhance sustainable development.
Our mission To promote human rights and minerals governance, campaign for environmental sustainability, enhance sustainable livelihoods of marginalized people in society including women, girls, youth and persons with disability for sustainable positive social change.
Core-Values 1. Respect for human rights and rule of Law 2. Passion for Nature 3. Transparency and Accountability 4. Responsiveness and Patriotism 5. Service 6. Diversity for sustainability 7. Team work and Partnership 8. Equity and inclusion 9. Social justice
Our Goal Research, documentation and dissemination, advocacy and campaigns, capacity-building <(>&<)> training, awareness creation, socialsupport services, lobbying and litigation for sustainable development.
StrategicObjectives 1. Advocacy and sensitization of communities on health, social and environmental issues. 2. Campaign for environmental sustainability and undertake tree planting exercises(aforestation and reforestation). 3. Provision of sustainable livelihood skills training and seed capital for, women, youth and people with disability. 4. Women and girls empowerment on their rights and inclusion-in decision-making process at all levels (home, community and nation). 5. Campaigns on civil rights 6. Climate Change Awareness creation and edification on resilience mitigation and adaptation using indigenous strategies 7. Community sensitization on peace and security 8. Research, documentation and dissemination 9. Promotion of community rights and good mineral governance.
